Level 3

Advanced

Python projects. 10 to 12 weeks, one session a week.

Thonny (or any editor), Terminal for git (Apple's free Command Line Tools; no GitHub account), Python standard library only (turtle, csv, random, collections, json), pytest.

0 of 12 weeks done on this device

Weekly lessons

  1. 1

    Week 1: Save Points: Git Basics

    Git is a save-game system for code: every commit is a save point you can go back to.

    Done
  2. 2

    Week 2: Objects: Blueprints and Things

    A class is a blueprint; objects are the things you build from it, and each one keeps its own data.

    Done
  3. 3

    Week 3: Families of Objects

    Child classes inherit from a parent and change only what is different; bigger objects are built from smaller ones.

    Done
  4. 4

    Week 4: Searching and How Fast Is Fast?

    Smart algorithms do less work: halving beats checking one by one.

    Done
  5. 5

    Week 5: Sorting, Stacks and Queues

    Sorting puts data in order; a stack remembers what to undo; a queue makes sure everyone gets a turn.

    Done
  6. 6

    Week 6: Review and Checkpoint

    Connect the pieces, and use the debugger to watch your code think, one line at a time.

    Done
  7. 7

    Week 7: Grids, Recursion and Fractal Art

    Functions that call themselves; worlds made of grids.

    Done
  8. 8

    Week 8: Data Detectives

    Data tells stories when you clean it, count it and chart it.

    Done
  9. 9

    Week 9: How Do Machines Learn?

    AI finds patterns in examples – and copies their mistakes.

    Done
  10. 10

    Week 10: Project Studio 1

    Design first: classes, data and milestones – then build the core.

    Done
  11. 11

    Week 11: Project Studio 2

    Test it, playtest it, polish it, explain it.

    Done
  12. 12

    Week 12: Showcase and Graduation

    Share what you built, explain your choices, and plan what comes next.

    Done

Final project: Build Something Big

Choose: (a) a grid game, (b) a generative art app, or (c) a data/AI app. Must use: at least 2 classes (one using inheritance or composition), a data structure beyond a flat list (dict, stack/queue or grid), one named algorithm (search/sort/recursion/BFS), a saved file, at least 5 pytest tests, and a git history with 8+ meaningful commits.
